summary: Transform your approach to water resource management with our expert training on economic instruments.
lede: Economic instruments for water resource management use tariffs, charges, permits and incentives to influence water use, service funding and pollution. For utility managers, finance teams, regulators and other water practitioners, the course addresses choosing tools suited to institutional conditions, designing tariffs and subsidies, and assessing affordability, conservation and pollution-control outcomes.
audienceIntro: This course is designed to empower a diverse range of professionals involved in water resource management. Whether you are managing utilities, setting tariffs, or implementing NGO programs, this training is tailored for you.
audience: Water utility managers, finance teams, and commercial
Basin authorities and watershed management institutions
Public sector staff in water, environment, finance
NGO WASH and climate resilience program leads
Economists, policy analysts, and M&E staff
modules: Foundations of Economic Instruments in Water Resource Management
Diagnosing the Real Problem Before Designing the Tool
Tariff Design for Water Supply and Sanitation Services
Cost Recovery and Financial Sustainability Without Public Backlash
Affordability, Equity, and Subsidy Targeting That Actually Works
Incentives for Conservation and Demand Management
Abstraction Charges, Allocation, and Managing Scarcity
Economic Appraisal and Scenario Modeling for Decision Support
Governance, Political Economy, and Stakeholder Buy-In
Reporting, Learning, and Proving Impact Over Time
prerequisites: Participants should have a basic understanding of water resource management and experience in related fields. Familiarity with economic principles and financial analysis is beneficial but not mandatory.
topics: Water & wastewater treatment and utility management
